'''Janne Wallenius''' is a [[Sweden|Swedish]] reactor physicist. He is a professor at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] (KTH) in [[Stockholm]], [[Sweden]].<ref>[https://www.kth.se/profile/janwal Profile]</ref>

Wallenius was born in 1968 in [[Trollhättan]], Sweden. At the age of 18, he won the particle physics contest on the Swedish television show "[[Kvitt eller dubbelt]]" (''Double or Nothing''), after which he was nicknamed "partikel-Janne".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=sv&u=http://www.nyteknik.se/nyheter/energi_miljo/karnkraft/article3367806.ece&prev=search|title=The Wild Party in the Reactor Hall|last=Karlsberg|first=Lars Anders|date=December 13, 2011|work=NYTeknik|accessdate=3 June 2015}}</ref> He studied Engineering Physics at [[Chalmers University of Technology]] in [[Gothenburg]] from 1987 to 1992. He got his PhD degree in Quantum Chemistry from [[Uppsala University]] in 1996.

In 2008 he was promoted to full professor at KTH.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://segate.sunet.se/cgi-bin/wa?A2=kth-ekot;FjHdxw;20080421185417%2B0200|title = LISTSERV 15.5 - Archives - Error}}</ref>

In 2013, he co-founded the company [[Blykalla]] ("Lead Cold") which designs small [[lead-cooled fast reactor]]s called SEALER intended for commercial power production in arctic communities. Blykalla has been listed as one of the 71 hottest start-ups in Sweden.<ref>[http://www.va.se/nyheter/2015/05/29/71-heta-svenska-startups/ Veckans Affärer, 29:e maj 2015]</ref>

In 2016 Wallenius appointed one of Sweden's 10 most innovative entrepreneurs by Foundation ÅForsk and Swedish Incubators & Science Parks.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mynewsdesk.com/se/uppsala_innovation_centre_ab/pressreleases/janne-wallenius-utsedd-till-en-av-sveriges-10-mest-innovativa-entreprenoerer-1363801|title=Janne Wallenius appointed one of Sweden's 10 most innovative entrepreneurs|date=April 6, 2016|accessdate=January 3, 2017}}</ref>

In 2022, Janne Wallenius received the [https://www.kth.se/en/om/innovation/om/the-kth-innovation-award-1.1045123 KTH Innovation Award], that aims to celebrate people from KTH who with creativity, grit and courage have contributed to solving society’s challenges with their innovations. The monetary award is 500 000 SEK.
